prompt: Build a small Python 3 standard-library-only sales-report project. Deliver main.py, README.md and self-tests in the current project directory. main.py reads CSV from stdin with exactly the header region,item,quantity,unit_cents. Use CSV quoting correctly, including commas and doubled quotes in item values. Quantities and prices are nonnegative decimal integers; blank physical lines may occur, and the input otherwise satisfies the format. Sum quantity*unit_cents by region, including regions whose total is zero. Print one line per region, sorted by the region's case-sensitive string value, as region followed by a TAB and its integer total cents. Region values contain no tabs or newlines. An input containing only the header produces no output. Do not use binary floating-point money or third-party packages. Document the input/output contract and include self-tests for quoted fields, repeated regions, zero totals and empty data. Keep all writes inside this project and do not access the network. Run your self-tests before finishing.

prompt: Build a Python 3 standard-library-only structured-log summarizer with main.py, README.md and self-tests. Read stdin as independent lines. A valid line has exactly this grammar: service=<name> level=<level> ms=<duration>, with one ASCII space between fields, name matching [A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*, level one of INFO,WARN,ERROR, and duration one or more ASCII decimal digits. Ignore invalid lines, including blank lines and lines with leading or trailing spaces. For each service appearing in any valid line, count valid entries, sum durations and count ERROR entries. Print services sorted case-sensitively, each as service<TAB>count<TAB>total_ms<TAB>errors, followed by invalid<TAB>N on its own final line. The service name 'invalid' is legal and remains an ordinary service row before the final invalid-line row. An empty input prints only invalid<TAB>0. Preserve exact matching boundaries; do not partially accept a malformed line. Document and test valid, invalid, repeated-service and empty inputs. Keep writes in this project, use no network, and run your tests.

prompt: Build a Python 3 standard-library-only fixed-width signed-integer codec with main.py, README.md and self-tests. Each nonblank stdin line is decimal_integer width byteorder separated by whitespace. Width is an integer from 1 through 32 inclusive, and byteorder is big or little; inputs satisfy that syntax. Process lines independently, skip whitespace-only lines and emit no headers. Support values beyond 64 bits without truncation. Test both byte orders, negative values, signed boundaries, overflow and widths above eight bytes. Document the contract. Keep all writes inside this project, use no network, and run self-tests before finishing.

prompt: Build a Python 3 standard-library-only postfix integer calculator with main.py, README.md and self-tests. Evaluate every stdin line independently as whitespace-separated tokens. prompt: Build a Python 3 standard-library-only literal template expander with main.py, README.md and self-tests. Each stdin line is a JSON object containing template (string) and values (mapping strings to strings). Scan the original template once from left to right. A doubled dollar sign $$ emits one literal dollar and consumes both characters. Otherwise ${name} replaces that entire token with values[name] only when name matches [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]* and exists in values; unknown but valid tokens stay unchanged. For a malformed token or unmatched dollar, emit the current character literally and continue scanning the next original character. Inserted values are never scanned again. Emit the result with json.dumps(ensure_ascii=True,separators=(',',':')), one JSON string per input line. Document the exact precedence and test adjacent tokens, $$ before braces, unknown names, malformed/unclosed braces and replacement values containing token syntax. Do not use eval, exec, external templates or third-party packages. Keep files in the project, use no network, and run self-tests.
